title: Deadman sentinel process for reliable span finalization on exit
description:
## Problem

OpenCode sessions are not reliably recorded in atuin because span finalization depends on `process.once("beforeExit", ...)` in [`src/plugin/hooks.ts`](src/plugin/hooks.ts). `beforeExit` only fires when the Node event loop empties *naturally* — it is **not** emitted on `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP`, `SIGKILL`, or hard crashes. OpenCode almost always exits via one of those signals (terminal close → `SIGHUP`, parent kill, Ctrl+C), so `finalizeAllForExit()` never runs. Even when it does run, the async `atuin history end` subprocess work has to complete before the process is torn down, and the detached-spawn fallback at `src/atuin/history-writer.ts:236` only triggers if the synchronous `end()` *fails* — not if we never reach exit code at all.

Root mistake: trying to do cleanup work *during the parent's own death*. Signal deaths don't give us a window.

## Solution: the deadman sentinel

Flip the model — do setup while the parent is **healthy** (at span start), and let cleanup fire *after* the parent is gone, triggered by an OS-level event (fd close), not by code running in a dying process.

### Mechanism (pipe-EOF trick)

1. On `history start` → we receive an `entryID`. **At that moment** spawn a deadman child:
   - `detached: true` (→ `setsid`, new session, survives terminal `SIGHUP`)
   - `stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "ignore"]` — parent holds the write end (`child.stdin`), child's fd 0 is the read end.
   - `child.unref()` so the parent can exit without waiting.
   - Spawned in the session's `envOverride` (ATUIN_SESSION) so the atuin call lands in the right scope.
2. The child runs an inline shell that blocks on `cat` (reads stdin forever).
3. When the parent dies for *any* reason — `SIGKILL`, crash, `SIGHUP`, clean exit — the kernel closes the parent's fds, the write end of the pipe closes, the child's `cat` sees **EOF**, unblocks, and runs `atuin history end <entryID> --exit <abortExitCode> --duration <now−startMs>`.
4. On a **normal** span end (idle/finalize), the parent itself runs `atuin history end`; on success it sends `SIGTERM` to the deadman, whose `trap 'exit 0' TERM` makes it die quietly without double-firing.

### Inline deadman script

```sh
trap 'exit 0' TERM              # parent cancelled us → normal end, do nothing
cat                             # block until parent dies (EOF on stdin)
atuin history end "$1" --exit "$2" --duration "$(($(date +%s%3N) - $3))"
```

Spawned via `spawn("sh", ["-c", script, "deadman", entryID, abortExitCode, startMs], ...)`.

This is bulletproof: detection is kernel-mediated (fd close), so it survives `SIGKILL`, crashes, laptop shutdown — everything. It cleanly replaces the current "detached fallback on failure" path: the deadman *is* the fallback, armed at start time rather than scrambled for at exit time.

## Scope (explicit non-goals)

- **NO reconciliation/sidecar file.** The deadman is the sole backstop. If the deadman itself is reaped (reboot), the span is lost — accepted.
- Keep the synchronous `end()` for the normal path; the deadman is a safety net, not the primary ender.
- `beforeExit`/detached-fallback code stays (harmless) but is no longer load-bearing.

## Implementation plan

- [ ] Add a `DeadmanRegistry` to `src/atuin/history-writer.ts`:
  - `arm(entryID, abortExitCode, startMs, envOverride)` → spawns the sentinel, stores `child.stdin` (write end) + child handle keyed by `entryID`.
  - `disarm(entryID)` → `child.kill("SIGTERM")`, drops the handle.
  - `disarmAll()` → teardown for any leftover at process end.
- [ ] Thread it through `AtuinHistoryWriter` — `start()` arms after a successful start; `end()` disarms on the normal (non-detached) success path.
- [ ] Wire `abortExitCode` and `startMs` through `AtuinOperationContext` so the deadman knows what to fire.
- [ ] Cover with tests in `test/`: simulate parent-death by closing the stdin handle and assert `atuin history end` runs; simulate normal end and assert the deadman is killed without firing.
- [ ] Update docs (`doc/arch.md`, `doc/spec/`, README exit-finalization section).

## Acceptance criteria

- Killing the host Node process with `SIGKILL` still results in an `atuin history end` entry being written (verified against the atuin DB).
- Normal idle/finalize ends the span synchronously AND disarms the deadman so no double `end` fires.
- Existing tests continue to pass; architecture invariants (`core/` stays process-free) hold.
- No new disk state, no sidecar file.

## References

- [`src/plugin/hooks.ts`](src/plugin/hooks.ts) — `beforeExit` wiring (currently load-bearing, will become vestigial)
- [`src/atuin/history-writer.ts`](src/atuin/history-writer.ts) — current detached fallback at `spawnDetachedEnd` / `end()` `duringExit` path
- [`src/plugin/session-span-tracker.ts`](src/plugin/session-span-tracker.ts) — `startSpan`/`endSpan`
- [`src/plugin/session-state.ts`](src/plugin/session-state.ts) — `pendingEntryID`/`pendingStartMs`

title: Deadman should emit a rich, self-describing 'where was I?' entry (title + context)
description:
## Why

The point of the deadman is a very easy-to-detect "where was I just now?" marker so the user can get back to a session fast. The user often has opencode sessions that dwell for multiple days before closing, so without a good report on the deadman-fired entry they'd have to go fishing for the atuin session id.

Today the deadman fires `atuin history end <entryID> --exit <abort> --duration <elapsed>`. The entry it closes has the **session id** baked in (`opencode -s <id>`, in command text and `--intent`), but **not the title**: a span's command is frozen at span-start, and spans usually start before a meaningful title exists. The title only lands on a *separate* title-stamp entry (when `title` mode is on). So the deadman-ended entry is self-describing only by session id, not by title.

## Complication: sessions switch and titles evolve

Sessions are interleaved (per-session deadmen), and a session's title updates over its lifetime. So the deadman needs to track the *latest* title for its session, not the title at span-start. Two families of approaches:

### A. Cycle (re-spawn) the deadman on title change
Re-spawn the sentinel with updated command args whenever the title changes. Title changes are edge-triggered today (`session-stamp-writer.maybeUpdateTitle` runs on every event that carries a title), so no poll timer is needed. Cost: one re-spawn per meaningful title change per session; re-spawns are cheap but multiply with interleaved sessions and frequent title churn.

### B. Stream updates to a long-lived deadman
Instead of baking context into spawn args and re-spawning, keep one long-lived sentinel per span and stream it update lines (new title, tmux session, etc.) that it records and replays when the parent dies. Avoids re-spawns and naturally carries evolving context. Open question: we previously rejected holding a managed Node stdin stream for *death detection* because OpenCode's JSC/Bun plugin runtime has no `child.stdin.unref()` and risks hanging the host on exit ([`oah-deadman-span-finalization`](.beads/issues.jsonl) notes). Streaming for *data updates* (while keeping PID polling for death detection) might be feasible via a named pipe / file / or a runtime-tolerant channel rather than a managed Node pipe. Needs investigation.

## Acceptance

- The deadman-fired entry (or a marker it writes when it fires) includes the **latest known title** for the session, in addition to the session id.
- Title updates are event-driven / edge-triggered (no poll timer introduced solely for the deadman).
- No regression to host-exit safety (never hang OpenCode; never keep a managed stream that the JSC/Bun runtime can't unref).

## References

- Current deadman: [`src/atuin/history-writer.ts`](src/atuin/history-writer.ts) `DEADMAN_SCRIPT` / `DeadmanRegistry`
- Title flow: [`src/plugin/session-stamp-writer.ts`](src/plugin/session-stamp-writer.ts) `maybeUpdateTitle`; [`src/core/command.ts`](src/core/command.ts) `formatResumeCommand`
- Related: [`oah-deadman-span-finalization`](.beads/issues.jsonl) (the PID-polling pivot notes explain why stdin streams are unsafe here)
- Companion: `oah-deadman-tmux-context` (wants tmux session in the comment too)

title: Establish plugin configuration architecture
description:
Define configuration as a first-class architectural boundary for opencode-atuin-hooks instead of treating settings as scattered environment-variable reads.

Problem: current configuration is parsed only from environment variables in `src/config/environment.ts`, while OpenCode also supports structured plugin tuple options. New features such as Atuin session scoping will add more settings, and without a clear position config risks leaking into plugin lifecycle code, Atuin writer code, command formatting, or intent metadata.

Goal: create a definite configuration model that says where config enters the system, how it is normalized, what precedence rules apply, and which modules may depend on runtime config. The result should preserve env-var compatibility while making tuple plugin options the documented primary structured mechanism.
design:
Architectural position:

- Treat config as a Functional Core boundary in `src/config/`, not as ad-hoc reads throughout the plugin.
- Read raw inputs at the plugin entry/shell boundary only: `process.env` plus OpenCode plugin tuple `options`.
- Normalize raw config once into a typed `PluginConfig` value before constructing runtime collaborators.
- Pass normalized config downward as explicit constructor/function arguments.
- Keep config parsing out of `SessionTracker`, core formatters, and `ShellAtuinHistory` except where writer options are already operational constructor inputs.
- Prefer tuple plugin options for structured settings because they are visible in `opencode.json` and supported by OpenCode's plugin loader.
- Preserve environment variables as compatibility fallbacks and for shell-oriented deployment.
- Establish precedence as: tuple options > environment variables > built-in defaults.
- Keep product metadata channels separate: config may control Atuin session scope behavior, but derived `ATUIN_SESSION` must not be mixed into command text or intent.

Likely implementation shape:

- Expand `readPluginConfig(env, options?)` to parse both env vars and `Record<string, unknown>` plugin options.
- Add small typed parsers for strings, booleans, numbers, hook mode arrays, and enum-like settings.
- Document supported option names and their env fallbacks.
- Update `opencode-atuin-hooks.ts` and `createAtuinHooks()` signatures to carry plugin options.
- Update architecture docs so config has an explicit place in the module map and data flow.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Architecture documentation states the plugin's configuration boundary, precedence order, and allowed module dependencies.
2) `PluginConfig` is the single normalized runtime config object constructed before `SessionTracker` and `ShellAtuinHistory` are created.
3) OpenCode tuple plugin options are supported for existing settings where practical, with env vars retained as fallbacks.
4) Config parsing remains deterministic and testable in `src/config/` without process spawning, hook mutation, or Atuin CLI behavior.
5) README documents both tuple options and env vars, including the precedence rule.
6) Tests cover defaults, env fallback behavior, tuple option precedence, invalid value fallback behavior, and hook mode parsing from both strings and arrays.
7) The later `oah-atuin-session-scope` work can add its mode setting through this config architecture without changing the architecture position again.
close_reason: Implemented configuration architecture with tuple option support, normalized PluginConfig boundary, documentation, and tests. Verified with pnpm test, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm run build.

title: Derive child ATUIN_SESSION scopes for opencode sessions
description:
Allow opencode-atuin-hooks to preserve the ambient terminal/window Atuin session hierarchy while recording each OpenCode logical session under a deterministic child `ATUIN_SESSION`.

Context: `zim-atuin-session` sets `ATUIN_SESSION` to deterministic terminal hierarchy values such as `tmux-<session_name>:<window_index>.<pane_index>`. This plugin can enrich Atuin's native session-scoping dimension by deriving a child value like `<ambient>/opencode/<opencodeSessionID>` for each atuin write.

Goal: make Atuin's session filter express both where work happened (tmux/window/pane) and which OpenCode logical session produced the entry, without moving this hierarchy into command text or intent metadata.
design:
- Add a pure formatter, likely `src/core/atuin-session.ts`, for deriving child Atuin session IDs from the ambient `ATUIN_SESSION` and OpenCode session ID.
- Preferred derived shape: `<ambient ATUIN_SESSION>/opencode/<sessionID>` when an ambient value exists; `opencode/<sessionID>` when no ambient value exists and child scoping is enabled.
- Add a writer-side environment override so `ShellAtuinHistory` can spawn `atuin` with a per-operation `ATUIN_SESSION` value.
- Treat `ATUIN_SESSION` as an operational Atuin session-scope channel, not intent metadata. Keep `session=...` in intent for search and diagnostics.
- Do not append tool call IDs to `ATUIN_SESSION`; tool calls should share the parent OpenCode session scope and place `call=...` in intent.
- Make behavior configurable to preserve migration safety. Candidate modes: `inherit` (use ambient value unchanged), `child` (derive child value), and possibly `replace` (use `opencode/<sessionID>` only).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A configurable mode controls Atuin session behavior, with documented default behavior.
2) In child mode, entries for OpenCode session `ses_x` spawned from ambient `ATUIN_SESSION=tmux-main:1.0` run atuin with `ATUIN_SESSION=tmux-main:1.0/opencode/ses_x`.
3) In inherit mode, the writer preserves the ambient `ATUIN_SESSION` exactly.
4) The derived Atuin session value is applied consistently to spans, stamps, exit finalization, and future tool-call entries for the same OpenCode session.
5) Intent formatting remains separate and still includes `session=ses_x`; command text remains `opencode -s ses_x` with optional title.
6) Tests cover ambient-present, ambient-missing, inherit mode, child mode, and tool-call sharing of the parent OpenCode session scope when tool calls are implemented.
notes: Closing: shipped. deriveAtuinSessionScope in src/core/atuin-session.ts, normalized as atuinSessionScope in src/config/environment.ts, wired as envOverrideForSessionID in src/plugin/hooks.ts. Strategies inherit/child/replace documented in README 'Atuin Session Scope'.

title: Separate history projection from atuin operations
description:
Refactor enrichment/history output so product metadata is prepared in a small pure core projection layer before reaching the atuin CLI writer.

Current state: enrichment is scattered across `hooks.ts` (`chat.message` user text capture), `event-session.ts` (message/model extraction), and `session-tracker.ts` (`intentFor()` private string formatting). `AtuinOperationContext` also carries the final `intent` string, which is fine, but it should remain an operational writer/logging context rather than grow into a product metadata bag.

Goal: preserve the useful command/intent split while making intent formatting independently testable and extensible for future message/model/tool/call metadata.
design:
- Add `src/core/intent.ts` as a pure functional-core module with `IntentField`, `IntentData`, and `formatIntent()`.
- Keep command text and intent separate: `src/core/command.ts` formats human resume/search command text; `src/core/intent.ts` formats searchable context metadata.
- Have `SessionTracker` assemble `IntentData` from known session facts (`lastUserText`, session ID, message ID, model) and pass only the formatted intent string into `AtuinOperationContext`.
- Keep `AtuinOperationContext` operational: event type, session ID, reason, exit timing, and already-formatted intent. Do not add product fields like `messageID`, `model`, `toolName`, `callID`, or tool args to the writer context.
- Route `chat.message` state mutation through the same serialized queue as event handling so all tracker mutation follows one ordering boundary.
- Update tests/docs to show the end-state map: projection in `src/core/*`, lifecycle state in `src/plugin/*`, CLI boundary in `src/atuin/*`.
acceptance_criteria:
1) `formatIntent()` is covered by focused unit tests for summary truncation, null omission, field ordering, and existing session/message/model output.
2) `SessionTracker` no longer contains private intent string-concatenation logic; it delegates formatting to `src/core/intent.ts`.
3) Existing session intent behavior is preserved: user text prefix, session ID, message ID, model, and 80-character summary truncation.
4) `chat.message` updates to tracker state are serialized through the existing queue in `hooks.ts`.
5) `AtuinOperationContext` remains an operational writer context and does not become a broad product metadata model.
6) Architecture tests or documentation cover the boundary: command text for human resume/search, intent for searchable metadata, atuin writer for CLI projection only.
close_reason: Implemented history projection architecture with pure intent formatter, serialized chat.message enrichment updates, tests, typecheck, and review fix.

title: Add zsh completion for opencode session IDs
description: Add zsh tab completion for opencode session IDs. When a user types an opencode command that takes a session ID argument, pressing Tab should complete available session IDs. This would likely integrate with atuin's session history to enumerate known session IDs and provide them as completion candidates.

title: Add zsh prompt on process exit to report last opencode session usage time
description:
When an opencode session exits, display a zsh prompt hook that reports the last time the opencode session was active/used. This gives users visibility into when their last session interaction occurred, helping them track session freshness and activity.

This would hook into the opencode process exit to record the timestamp, then surface it via a zsh precmd or chpwd hook so the user sees the last-session-time in their shell prompt after returning from opencode.

title: Record tool calls as atuin history entries
description:
Add a hook mode that records tool invocations in atuin history with parameters represented as command arguments. Include support for abstracting prompt interactions as a `question` tool event with normalized args and captured answers. Track real per-tool duration where available so history reflects actual execution time rather than only zero-duration stamps.

Stretch behavior: support optional deep tracing mode that emits entries for intermediate thinking/update events so users can inspect fine-grained session activity in atuin.

Architecture direction: build this on top of the history projection boundary from `opencode-atuin-hooks-history-projection`. Tool calls should be a second history projection path, not extra fields bolted onto session entries. They should reuse shared intent formatting for metadata while using their own command-text formatter for human/searchable tool invocation records.
design:
- Introduce a new tool-event mode that listens for tool call/update events and emits one atuin entry per completed tool invocation.
- Normalize command shape to keep atuin search useful and avoid storing large JSON blobs as a single opaque token.
- Special-case prompt interactions (single choice / multi-choice / freeform) under a synthetic `question` tool name with structured args+answers.
- Use start/end pairing to capture duration when a tool run has clear begin/end timestamps; fall back to duration=0 when only terminal event exists.
- Keep defaults conservative to avoid noisy history; deep tracing is opt-in.
- Add a pure `src/core/tool-command.ts` formatter for tool command text such as `opencode -s <sessionID> --tool <toolName> [--arg <key>=<value> ...]`.
- Reuse `src/core/intent.ts` for cross-cutting metadata such as `session`, `message`, `model`, `tool`, and `call`; do not make `AtuinOperationContext` carry raw product metadata.
- Add `src/plugin/tool-tracker.ts` only when real pending tool call state is needed. It should own pending call IDs and durations separately from `SessionTracker`.
- Tool calls should share the parent OpenCode session's derived `ATUIN_SESSION` scope when `oah-atuin-session-scope` is enabled; do not append call IDs to `ATUIN_SESSION`.
- Keep session records and tool records distinct: session records answer what OpenCode session existed or was active; tool records answer what specific tool invocation happened.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A tool invocation produces an atuin entry with command text that includes tool name and normalized args.
2) Question interactions are represented as a `question` tool entry including prompt metadata and selected answers.
3) Duration is non-zero when start/end timing can be derived from events; otherwise records safely with duration=0.
4) The feature is gated by explicit mode/config and does not change current default behavior.
5) Documentation describes command format, redaction limits, and expected event sources.
6) Tool command text is produced by a pure core formatter, not by `SessionTracker` or `ShellAtuinHistory`.
7) Tool intent metadata is produced through shared intent formatting and includes `session`, `tool`, and `call` fields when available.
8) `AtuinOperationContext` remains operational and does not grow tool-specific product fields such as raw args, `toolName`, or `callID`.
9) Tool entries use the same OpenCode-session-level `ATUIN_SESSION` scope as their parent session when session scoping is configured.
10) Tests cover at least one session entry and one tool entry in the same OpenCode session to prove the command text differs while shared metadata/scope stays coherent.
notes:
Assessment before update: existing ticket already had valuable scope for normalized argv-shaped tool entries, synthetic `question` records, real duration when possible, zero-duration fallback, opt-in/deep tracing, and redaction documentation. This update preserves that material and adds the accepted architecture constraints: tool calls build on the shared history projection boundary, reuse intent formatting, keep their own command formatter, keep pending tool state out of `SessionTracker`, and avoid turning `AtuinOperationContext` into a product metadata model.
Closing: shipped. ToolCallTracker (src/plugin/tool-call-tracker.ts) records tool calls via history start/end; shell mode records bash calls, tool mode is the superset. formatToolCommand in src/core/tool-command.ts; toolResultComment option adds result context. Documented in README 'Behavior Modes' and doc/tool-call-history.md.

title: Embed model and message ID as comments in atuin command
description: Append metadata as comments to the atuin command entry: model name, opencode message update ID. These provide additional context when reviewing atuin history.
notes: Message ID is now captured via --intent (session=<id> message=<id>). Remaining scope: add model=<modelName> to the intent string. Model info may need to come from session/message events if available on the event bus.

title: Capture cwd by spawning atuin from session working directory
description: Spawn atuin commands from the session's working directory so atuin records the correct cwd. This ensures `opencode -s <id>` entries appear with the right project path in atuin search.

title: Capture session title/description in atuin command text
description: Parse the session title/description and append it as a comment in the atuin history entry command text, e.g. `opencode -s ses_xxx # refactoring auth`. This makes atuin search results more informative.

title: opencode-atuin-hooks enhancements
description: Enhancements to the opencode-atuin-hooks plugin for richer atuin history entries and improved configurability.
notes: Closing: all 4 children complete (atuin-session-scope ✓, config-architecture ✓, tool-call-history ✓, history-projection ✓).

title: Deadman-fired entry should include tmux session in the comment
description:
## Why

When the deadman fires (opencode exited / crashed), the user wants to know not just *what* session they were in (title + opencode session id) but *where* — which tmux session/pane. The user often has many long-dwelling opencode sessions across tmux; an earlier identifier (tmux session name) in the deadman-fired entry's comment makes "where was I?" much faster to answer, especially for sessions that sat for days.

## What

On the deadman-fired entry only (normal entries are unaffected), append the tmux session context to the command comment, e.g.:

```text
opencode -s <sessionID>  # <title> [tmux: <session>]
```

## Notes

- Deadman-only: the title/id stay as-is for normal span/stamp entries; only the deadman-fired marker carries the tmux context.
- Depends on the mechanism from `oah-deadman-title-context` for how evolving context (title, and now tmux session) reaches the deadman. Likely rides the same stream/cycle plumbing once that lands.
- tmux session can be read from `TMUX` / `$TMUX_PANE` / `tmux display-message -p '#S'` at deadman-spawn time (cheap, env-snapshot), or streamed if we go with the streaming architecture.

## Acceptance

- Deadman-fired entry's command comment includes the tmux session name (when available).
- Normal entries are unchanged.
- Graceful no-op when not running under tmux.

## References

- Depends on: `oah-deadman-title-context`
- Current deadman: [`src/atuin/history-writer.ts`](src/atuin/history-writer.ts)

title: Zsh exit hook: print opencode session summary on quit
description: A zsh hook (or similar shell integration) that detects when an opencode process exits and prints a session summary to the terminal. Summary should include the session title, the first user request, and the last assistant response. Gives the user immediate context about what just happened without needing to open atuin or re-enter opencode.
design:
- Hook into zsh's TRAPCHLD or use a process-monitor approach to detect opencode exit.
- Read session data from atuin history (filtered by author=opencode, most recent session) or from opencode's own state.
- Extract: title (from atuin intent or opencode state), first user message, last assistant response.
- Print a compact summary block to stdout.
- Could be a standalone zsh function in zim-atuin or a companion to the opencode-atuin-hooks plugin.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hook triggers when opencode process exits (detectable via TRAPCHLD or similar).
2) Prints session title, first user message summary, and last assistant response to stdout.
3) Gracefully handles missing session data (no title, no messages).
4) Configurable output format (compact vs verbose).
5) Works alongside existing opencode-atuin-hooks plugin.
